segments.label: Launch & ascent — Kennedy Space Center LC-39A
segments.note: SpaceX Falcon 9 from Kennedy Space Center LC-39A (28.608°, -80.604°); ~9 min analytic ascent to a 185 km parking orbit (schematic arc, real pad and launch time).

segments.label: Parking orbit coast
segments.note: Circular 185 km parking orbit, inclination 29.4° (plane through the pad at launch and the Moon at arrival — the launch-window geometry). Coast 135 min to the trans-lunar injection burn.

segments.label: Trans-lunar coast (6.7 days)
segments.note: Two-body Lambert arc from the TLI point to the modeled LOI point (Moon's position from the ephemeris at LOI). Departure Δv 3137 m/s, arrival v∞ 0.99 km/s. Mid-course corrections not modeled.

segments.label: Lunar orbit (~92 km, 17.8 rev)
segments.note: Circular orbit after LOI (published 100 km; modeled 92 km so that the orbit reaches the descent-orbit-insertion point exactly at DOI). Plane contains the arrival asymptote and the landing site; inclination 168.4°.

segments.label: Descent orbit (92 × 15 km)
segments.note: Descent-orbit insertion lowers perilune to 15 km opposite the powered-descent point; 0.5 revolutions to PDI (DOI modeled at 2026-10-28T10:48:03Z).

segments.label: Powered descent & landing
segments.note: Powered descent integrated for the lander class (Nova-C class (Intuitive Machines): 4.0 kN, Isp 340 s, 1622 kg at PDI): 15.1 min, Δv 2000 m/s. Model, not telemetry. Published duration ≈12 min.

events.title: Launch — Kennedy Space Center LC-39A · SpaceX Falcon 9
Powered descent initiation (15 min, 772 km downrange)

notes: Projected route: the provider's previous flight profile applied to the announced window; dates are illustrative until the launch is scheduled.

IM-3 (Reiner Gamma) is planned for the second half of 2026 on a Falcon 9 from KSC LC-39A. Route projected from the IM-1/IM-2 profile (direct ~6.5-day transfer, ~1–3 days in lunar orbit) on an illustrative date.
TLI placed at 2026-10-20T06:24:02Z (published/nominal 2026-10-20T04:45:00Z): the point on the parking orbit was chosen for a tangential departure toward the Moon.
